Flat orthographic game texture concept: one face of a heavy hewn oak beam from the timber frame of a house in a damp late-medieval harbour town, seen straight on; camera perpendicular, no perspective, no rounded shading, flat even shadowless light. The face is an upright band exactly half as wide as tall, 768 by 1536 pixels, centred on the canvas with plain light grey margins left and right; it fills the band edge to edge.

[FORM — keep exactly] One solid squared timber, dressed flat with an adze: fine straight lengthwise grain and faint shallow adze marks, no bark, no wavy grain. Three dark shrinkage cracks along the grain, of different lengths: one runs nearly the whole length, two are shorter and stop partway; they are narrow and slightly irregular. One thin flat hand-forged iron strap across the beam about a quarter of the way down from the top, its height about a tenth of the band width, plain dull iron with rust, two small flat nail heads near its two ends.

[COLOUR AND AGEING] The darkest wood in town: very dark olive brown, mean colour close to sRGB 41, 35, 21, low saturation. Damp from the sea: large flat dark olive damp stains, a few soft dark green patches in and beside the cracks, a dull rust stain below the strap. Old and wet but sound.

[STYLE] Painterly but readable material reference; the look of a dark late-medieval game from the early 2000s, remade with better craft; muted, low saturation, low contrast; clean surface without generator noise, white specks or scale-like stroke patterns.

[AVOID — rejected before] Bark, wavy flowing grain, scaly strokes. Bright yellow-green moss clumps. A beam that reads as planks. A thick band, domed rivets, a tread pattern on the iron. Light or saturated wood. Painted light and shadow. Text, people, props.
